# RANKED ACTION PLAN — synthesis of 72 findings

## Deduplication map

The 72 findings collapse into 9 distinct mechanisms (reader agreement noted — 4-5 independent readers converged on the top 3, which raises confidence):

| Cluster | Merged findings | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Join output rework** | 8, 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 21, 22, 23, 26(join), 35, 40(join), 44, 53, 54, 56, 64 | Row-major build payload + salt-tagged u64 entries + probe side never gathered + dict emission |
| **B. Direct-address join** | 17, 36(b), 55 | No hash table for dense int build keys (footer stats gated) |
| **C. Dictionary end-to-end** | 2, 3, 5, 20, 27, 34, 42, 45, 59, 60, plus expr-cache 40 | Preserve parquet dictionaries; filter/agg/join on codes; cache by dictionary identity |
| **D. Agg state rewrite** | 24, 25, 26(agg), 30, 31, 32, 37, 38, 46, 61, 62, 63, 66 | Fixed-stride rows, inline states, stored hash, radix Abandon merge |
| **E. Selection/late-mat filters** | 4, 29, 33, 36, 39, 47, 48, 57, 65 | Filter-cols-first decode, sel in hot triangle, ALWAYS_TRUE zone maps, adaptive conjunct order |
| **F. Scan micro-wins** | 6, 10, 11, 43(cache), 52 | Footer cache, buffer reuse, prefetch coalescing, decoded-batch cache |
| **G. Utf8View strings** | 1, 9, 51 | 16-byte German-string views engine-wide |
| **H. Bloom into decode** | 19, 58 | Join bloom filter evaluated inside RowFilter (we have post-decode bitmap filters already — the delta is decode-time application only) |
| **I. Sidecar (B5)** | 12, 42, 49, 50, 51, 65(storage) | Design calibration for the planned Arrow IPC mmap cache |

**Skepticism applied.** Summing the readers' estimates gives >5s of "savings" against a total gap of 4.7s (8.8 → 4.1 like-for-like). The estimates double-count: dict emission, row-arena gather, and probe-side zero-copy all claim the same 60-70% gather share; Utf8View and dictionary preservation claim the same string columns; sidecar claims all of B1 that findings 2/4/6 also claim. My ranked payoffs below are de-overlapped. Findings I *discounted* because we already do them or evidence is weak: SIMD gather probes (explicitly refuted by VLDB'18 Fig 9), probe-side dict key caching (TPC-H joins are int-keyed), FSST anywhere (DuckDB itself ships `enable_fsst_vectors=false`), prefetch cost model (we're on warm NVMe page cache), HLL adaptation (do the cheap proxy only, after D lands), bitpacking segment format (SF=100 insurance only).

---

## The ranked plan

| # | Item | Effort | De-overlapped payoff | Cluster |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Quick join bundle: probe-side zero-copy, `has_duplicate_keys` flag, salt entries, CRC hash | 3-4 d | −0.4 to −0.6s | A (cheap half) |
| 2 | Dictionary end-to-end (scan coercion + dict-identity agg cache + dict-level filters) | 4-5 d | −0.35 to −0.55s | C |
| 3 | Direct-address join for dense int keys | 2-3 d | −0.3 to −0.5s | B |
| 4 | Row-major build arena + typed row gather + partitioned build (kills concat) | 6-9 d | −0.5 to −0.8s (on top of #1) | A (expensive half) |
| 5 | Scan/filter cheap-wins bundle (footer cache, ALWAYS_TRUE zonemaps, all-pass/all-fail filter passthrough, adaptive conjunct order) | 3 d | −0.25 to −0.45s | E+F |
| 6 | Agg row layout + radix Abandon merge | 6-9 d | −0.3 to −0.5s | D |
| 7 | Filter-first two-phase decode (payload cols decoded through RowSelection; skip on zero) | 4-6 d | −0.15 to −0.3s | E |
| 8 | Sidecar v0: Arrow IPC mmap, dict strings, per-chunk zone maps | 10-15 d | −0.8 to −1.2s of *remaining* B1 | I |
| 9 | Bloom filter into RowFilter decode path | 2-3 d | −0.1 to −0.2s | H |
| 10 | Utf8View migration | 1.5-2 wk | mostly subsumed by #2/#8; do only if Q13/comment-heavy still lags | G |

Items 1+2+3+5 = ~2 weeks for an estimated −1.3 to −2.0s (8.8 → ~7.0s). Items 4+6+7 take the projected total to ~5.5-6.0s. Item 8 is the path below DuckDB-parquet 4.1s.

---

## Top 6 implementation plans

### 1. Quick join bundle (probe zero-copy + build-unique flag + salt entries + CRC hash)

**What.** Four small changes to `src/physical/operators/hash_join.rs` (+ `vectorized_hash.rs`):
- **(a)** Track `has_duplicate_keys: bool` during build (we already detect key-equal collisions when threading duplicates). When false — every PK build: orders, part, supplier, customer, nation — skip the chain-follow/match-count bookkeeping in `probe_vectorized()`.
- **(b)** Probe-side output: when `has_duplicate_keys == false` and the matched probe indices are the identity 0..n (full match, common for FK joins after semi-reduction), `Arc::clone` the probe ArrayRefs into the output batch instead of `compute::take` (the take at hash_join.rs:1708, 2574; note 2562 already does this for one Q09 path — generalize it to all probe paths). When not identity, verify a single shared `UInt32Array` of indices is built once and reused for all probe columns (1708 does this; audit 1613/2060/2404 paths).
- **(c)** Replace `VectorizedHashTable`'s (u32,u32) heads/next/entries triple with a single `Vec<u64>` of `salt16 | row_index48` (DuckDB `ht_entry.hpp` constants: SALT_MASK top 16 bits, load factor 2.0, salt check only when capacity > 8192). Compare salt before touching key data; keep chains via a next-slot array. Restructure probe as DuckDB's 3-phase loop (tag-scan → batched key verify → retry collided) so multi-col/string keys stop doing per-candidate dynamic downcasts.
- **(d)** Swap hash to hardware CRC32 (`_mm_crc32_u64` x2, VLDB'18: up to 40% on memory-bound joins from shortening the pre-load dependency chain).

**Correctness risks.** (b): identity detection must account for NULL keys and filtered probe rows — gate on `matched_count == probe_rows` exactly. (c): 48-bit index overflow is impossible (we cap builds far below 2^48) but salt-region collision handling must preserve the wrap semantics; the swapped Semi/Anti paths (per MEMORY.md these were buggy before) need the full spill_tests + duckdb_validated suites.

**Acceptance.** Q09 1.51s → ≤1.30s; Q21 868ms → ≤750ms; Q13 563ms → ≤500ms; all 156 duckdb_validated tests cell-exact; Q17/Q20 (semi/anti swapped) unchanged results.

### 2. Dictionary end-to-end

**What.**
- `src/storage/parquet.rs` + `streaming_parquet_scan.rs`: schema-coerce low-NDV string columns to `Dictionary(Int32, Utf8)` via `ArrowReaderBuilder` schema override. Detect from footer: dictionary_page_offset present + small dict. Target columns: l_returnflag, l_linestatus, l_shipmode, l_shipinstruct, o_orderpriority, o_orderstatus, p_brand, p_type, p_container, n_name, r_name. arrow-rs reuses one values `Arc` for all batches of a column chunk — `Arc::as_ptr(values)` is the free "dictionary id."
- `src/physical/morsel_agg.rs` (state) + `operators/morsel_agg.rs`: replace per-batch dict remap tables with a cache `dict_ptr → Vec<u32 group_slot>` (DuckDB `TryAddDictionaryGroups`, thresholds: dict ≤ 20000, or anonymous dict if 2·dict_size < batch rows). Once resolved_count == dict_size, per-row cost = one array index. Multi-dict keys: pack `(code1 << k) | code2` and route to the existing perfect-hash/dense path (Q01's two flags = ≤16 combos; extends finding 31's stats-based bit packing to dict codes).
- `src/physical/operators/filter.rs`: dict fast path for string predicates — evaluate LIKE/IN/= once over `values()` into a `Vec<bool>` cached by dict_ptr; row mask = byte lookup per key. (DuckDB `dictionary_decoder.cpp` Filter.)
- Guard: any operator that can't consume DictionaryArray falls back via lazy `take` — audit project/sort/join key extraction.

**Correctness risks.** Dictionary values Arc identity is per-column-chunk in arrow-rs — must not cache across files/row groups without checking pointer identity per batch. CAST/comparison semantics on dict arrays in arrow-rs kernels (nulls in keys vs null slot in values). RowFilter interplay: coerced schema must match projection masks.

**Acceptance.** Q01 427ms → ≤330ms (decode + group-key path); Q16 286ms → ≤220ms; Q19 353ms → ≤300ms; Q12 274ms → ≤240ms. Cell-exact on all 22.

### 3. Direct-address join

**What.** New path in `hash_join.rs` gated in `physical/planner.rs`: inner (+ semi) join, single int equality key, footer `(max−min) ≤ ~4M`, stats valid (no build-side filter that invalidates them — or check range at build time and bail). Build: `Vec<u32>` slots of row_index+1 (0 = empty) + dup-bit; bail to normal HJ on duplicate (or keep a side chain). Probe = subtract min, bounds check, load — no hashing, no salt, no compare. We already have the dense-domain machinery from the Q18 direct-address agg and footer min/max in the CBO, so this is mostly wiring. TPC-H PK domains are dense: n_nationkey(25), s_suppkey(100K), c_custkey(1.5M), p_partkey(2M) all qualify at SF=10; at SF=100 partkey (20M range = 80MB) needs the cap raised or gated on memory budget.

**Correctness risks.** Stats trust: parquet footer min/max must reflect the *build input after filters* — safest is compute exact min/max during build (one pass we already make) and never trust the footer for the range, only for the *decision*. NULL keys (skip). Runtime duplicate detection must bail cleanly to the standard build without losing rows.

**Acceptance.** Q09 (part+supplier joins over 6.6M rows) −150 to −250ms; Q05/Q07/Q08 −30 to −80ms each; Q02 122ms → ≤100ms. Verify fallback triggers correctly by forcing a duplicate-key dimension in a unit test.

### 4. Row-major build arena (the big B2 rewrite)

**What.** In `hash_join.rs`, for joins with ≥3 build output columns:
- Build: threads scatter rows into thread-local paged arenas (256KB pages), layout per DuckDB `TupleDataLayout::Initialize`: `[validity bytes][key cols][payload cols packed, Utf8 as (u32 len, 4B prefix, u64 ptr into string heap arena)][next/hash u64]`. Store the 64-bit hash in the next slot during sink; finalize overwrites it with the chain pointer (never rehash). Merge = `Vec::append` of page lists — **deletes the `concat_batches` at hash_join.rs:597** (hundreds of MB of memcpy on Q09) and the >2GB Utf8-offset concat failure mode. Finalize: rayon over row ranges CAS-inserting `salt|row_addr` into one `AtomicU64` table (this replaces #1c's index table with addresses; #1c's probe shape carries over unchanged).
- Probe output: replace per-column `gather_column`/`compute::take` (1074, 1700, 2651+) with one typed loop per column reading `row_ptr + offset` — one cache miss per matched *row* instead of per row *per column*. Strings ≤48B stay within the touched lines.
- Semi/Anti/Right matched-flag becomes a byte in the row (removes the separate AtomicBool stream).
- Keep the columnar path for 1-2-column outputs and for the spill path (SpillableHashJoinExec untouched initially); the 16-way radix partitioning of arenas becomes the future unified spill unit.

**Correctness risks.** Highest-risk item in the plan: unsafe offset arithmetic, string heap lifetime, endianness of packed validity, Right/Full sweep resumability, and the spill path must keep producing identical results (spill_tests.rs). Land behind a width-gate so 2-col joins exercise the old path continuously.

**Acceptance.** Q09 1.30s (post-#1) → ≤0.95s; Q18 1.43s → ≤1.15s; Q20 1.11s → ≤0.90s; Q21 → ≤0.65s. Memory: peak RSS on Q09 must *drop* (no concat copy). All spill tests pass at tiny limits.

### 5. Scan/filter cheap-wins bundle

**What.**
- **Footer metadata cache** (`storage/parquet.rs`): global `OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<(path, mtime), Arc<ParquetMetaData>>>>`. We currently re-parse 8 footers per query. ~1 day.
- **ALWAYS_TRUE zone maps**: we prune ALWAYS_FALSE row groups; add the other side — when footer min/max *proves* a predicate for a whole row group, drop it from the per-batch filter for that group's batches (DuckDB `CheckZonemap` SetFilterAlwaysTrue). Q01's `shipdate <=` is ALWAYS_TRUE for ~95% of row groups and we evaluate it on 60M rows anyway. ~1 day.
- **Filter passthrough** (`operators/filter.rs`): if `mask.true_count() == len`, forward the batch (no filter kernel); if 0, drop. Hours of work; removes Q01's near-total-pass compaction copy.
- **Adaptive conjunct ordering**: split top-level AND, evaluate conjunct k only where earlier conjuncts passed (boolean-mask chaining is fine, no sel needed: evaluate on the compacted survivor batch after the *first* conjunct only if selectivity < 50%, else mask-and). Copy DuckDB's constants (5 warmup / 20 execute / 10 observe / likeliness halving) for order learning; apply the same permutation to RowFilter predicate order. 1-2 days.

**Correctness risks.** ALWAYS_TRUE requires exact min/max semantics with NULLs (parquet stats null_count handling) — only apply for non-null columns or when null_count==0. Conjunct reordering must not reorder across short-circuit-dependent predicates (we have no side-effecting predicates, so safe).

**Acceptance.** Q06 122ms → ≤90ms; Q01 −40 to −70ms; every query −5 to −15ms fixed (footer cache) — measurable as Q11 178ms → ≤160ms, Q22 431ms → ≤400ms even with nothing else.

### 6. Aggregation row layout + radix Abandon merge

**What.** Two stages in `morsel_agg.rs` (state) + `operators/morsel_agg.rs` + `hash_agg.rs`:
- **Stage 1 (layout):** plan-time `AggLayout { key_width, hash_offset, acc_offsets, stride }`; replace `HashMap<u64, Vec<AccumulatorState>>` (morsel_agg.rs:32, 306) with `Vec<u64>` pointer table (`salt16|arena_offset48`) over paged `Vec<u8>` arenas; states inline (SUM f64=8B, AVG=16B, Welford=24B); the 64-bit hash stored in-row so resize/merge never rehashes. String keys ≤16B packed inline as u128 (ClickHouse tiering); longer via per-partition bump arena. Emit output by walking arenas sequentially. This deletes the profiled "per-group Vec heap boxes / entry movement dominated merges."
- **Stage 2 (radix merge):** cap thread-local tables at 32K entries (262144 if ≤2 threads); rows partitioned at insert by hash bits 48−k..48 (k = min(log2(threads),4), max 8, disjoint from salt and slot-index bits); on fill, **Abandon**: clear pointer table, keep partition buffers, continue. Global merge = move buffers; rayon task per partition rebuilds an exact-sized table from stored hashes. Add the cheap adaptation proxy: after 1M rows, if groups/rows > 0.95 switch to append-only (skip probing), dedup at finalize.
- Keep the perfect-hash ≤256 path and the dense direct-address path exactly as they are — this replaces only the HashMap fallback tier.

**Correctness risks.** Accumulator NULL semantics in raw bytes (validity bit per state); DISTINCT aggregates and multi-arg aggregates (APPROX_PERCENTILE second_arg) don't fit fixed-stride cleanly — route those to the old path. HAVING-inside-merge (existing per-shard optimization) must be re-plumbed onto partition finalize.

**Acceptance.** Q13 563ms → ≤430ms; Q10 894ms → ≤730ms; Q16 → ≤230ms (composes with #2); Q18 unchanged (dense path untouched); stddev/variance tests cell-exact.

---

## The four explicit questions

**(a) Row-major vs columnar payloads?** Row-major for the two materialized states — join build payload (when ≥3 output columns) and aggregate group rows — and columnar everywhere data streams. The evidence is unusually strong: DuckDB, ClickHouse, and Photon independently converged on row-major materialized state, and it targets exactly our profiled costs (gather = 60-70% of probe wall because per-column `take` costs ~1 random miss per row *per column*; agg merges dominated by per-group heap-box movement). Keep keys columnar during vectorized hash/compare (our i64 fast path stays), keep probe side columnar always, and keep the columnar take path for narrow (1-2 col) build outputs where row transposition loses.

**(b) Selection-vector retrofit?** **No general retrofit; yes to three surgical pieces.** The VLDB'18 data actually argues *against* a full retrofit for us: below ~50% selectivity everything is memory-bound and compaction is one linear copy of survivors — cheap; and Photon's position lists pay off mostly because their whole kernel library is templated on them, which arrow-rs's is not. The real waste is at the extremes and at the scan boundary, so take: (1) all-pass/all-fail passthrough in FilterExec (free, plan #5); (2) filter-column-first decode where the "selection" lives inside arrow-rs `RowSelection` and never touches operator contracts (plan #7); (3) sel-aware *consumer loops only* in the fused scan→probe→agg triangle, where our accumulate/probe loops are already index-based — pass `(&RecordBatch, &[u32])` into them without inventing a SelBatch type that every operator must understand. Do not change the inter-operator batch contract; compact at pipeline breakers as today.

**(c) DuckDB's parquet speed: reader or integration?** ~70% integration, ~30% reader. The reader kernels (whole-batch memcpy PLAIN, hoisted bounds checks, all-valid RLE fast path) are maybe 1.5-2x over arrow-rs on fixed-width — real but not the story. The story is that decode *output feeds execution without re-materialization*: dictionaries decoded once per chunk and kept as codes through filter/agg/join; string bytes never copied (views into the page buffer); filter columns decoded once, payload columns skip-decoded through the surviving selection; no compaction kernel ever. arrow-rs users' cheapest 80%, in order: (1) dictionary schema coercion + dict-identity caches (plan #2 — no reader changes at all); (2) footer metadata cache; (3) ALWAYS_TRUE predicate dropping; (4) two-phase filter-first decode with RowSelection so RowFilter columns aren't decoded twice and zero-match batches skip payload decode; (5) Utf8View coercion for high-NDV strings (arrow-rs 53 supports view types; verify the parquet→view path avoids the copy in our version before investing). Writing our own decoder is *not* justified pre-sidecar; the sidecar (below) makes it moot.

**(d) Arrow IPC mmap sidecar vs lightweight-compressed format?** **Proceed with the sidecar — the findings validate it and sharpen the spec.** DuckDB-native's 4.1→2.94s win is *not* clever compression; it's (i) decode-free vector materialization, (ii) **stable dictionary identity** that unlocks the dict-aware join/agg/filter fast paths with zero per-query work, (iii) zone maps without page-header parsing. All three are exactly what mmap'd Arrow IPC gives us. v0 spec: uncompressed numerics 64-byte aligned (bandwidth math: Q01's 7 columns ≈ 2.3-2.8GB, 55-70ms at streaming rates — no bandwidth wall at SF=10, whole sidecar ~8GB fits page cache); low-NDV strings as IPC DictionaryArray (one dictionary per file → stable Arc, plan #2's caches hit forever); ~128K-row chunks matching morsel granularity; per-chunk min/max footer. Explicitly **skip FSST and general compression in v0** (DuckDB's own default keeps FSST vectors out of execution); add FOR+bitpacking/ALP only as a v1 SF=100 insurance policy when data exceeds RAM. One sequencing caveat: build the 2-day decoded-batch cache (finding F) first only if we care about warm multi-scan queries (Q15/Q20 read lineitem twice) — but don't let it masquerade as a benchmark win for cold-decode parity; the sidecar is the honest fix. Schedule the sidecar *after* plans 1-5: it eliminates B1, but plans 1-4 are what close the gap that remains even when DuckDB reads the same parquet (4.45s like-for-like), which is execution, not storage.

**Projected trajectory** (de-overlapped, conservative): plans 1+2+3+5 (~2 wks) → ~7.0s; +4+6 (~2 more wks) → ~5.7s; +7+9 → ~5.3s; +sidecar v0 → ~4.2-4.5s, i.e. at or below DuckDB-on-parquet with all 22 queries still cell-exact and memory-safe.

The 72 findings collapse into 9 distinct mechanisms (reader agreement noted — 4-5 independent readers converged on the top 3, which raises confidence):

| Cluster | Merged findings | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Join output rework** | 8, 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 21, 22, 23, 26(join), 35, 40(join), 44, 53, 54, 56, 64 | Row-major …
